text: IXIA Guardrails. Every client enquiry gets an answer in seconds, and the risky ones wait for a lawyer. We built it on Cloudflare Workers AI during the TechEx Amsterdam hackathon.

IXIA is our AI intake platform for law firms, immigration consultants and clinics. Speed wins clients. But in a regulated firm, an automatic reply can give advice on someone's own case, promise an outcome, invent a fee or a phone number, or repeat a diagnosis or an asylum case back by e-mail.

Guardrails puts a gate between the AI draft and the client. Inbound rules catch prompt injection and sensitive personal data. The draft is grounded in the firm's own knowledge base. Then two independent model checks and a set of fixed rules decide: send, hold for a human, or block. Every decision goes into a hash-chained audit log.

Four models run on Workers AI, each with one job. B G E M 3 retrieves knowledge across languages. Llama 3.3 seventy B writes the draft with citations. Llama Guard 3 classifies the reply. And G P T O S S one twenty B, a different model family, checks every claim against the knowledge base. The checks run in parallel.

Held does not mean silent. The client gets an instant acknowledgement in their own language, with no advice and none of their details, while the draft waits for a lawyer. Every AI-written message says that it was written by AI.

We measured it on {cases} hand-written enquiries in six languages, against the live models. {mh_auto} of {mh_n} sensitive or hostile enquiries got an automatic reply. Without the gate, all {mh_n} would have. {ms_auto} of {ms_n} plain questions were still answered instantly, with a median of {p50} seconds per enquiry.

For the firm, that is speed without losing control: an instant reply, a human on sensitive cases, six languages, and an audit trail a compliance officer can verify. Guardrails ships inside the IXIA subscription, at well under a tenth of a cent of model cost per enquiry. Now, the live demo.

A client asks what a first consultation costs. The lamps light up in the order the real checks finished. Every figure is in the knowledge base, so the reply goes out at once, signed, with the AI disclosure line.

Now a Dutch enquiry. An employee on sick leave with burn-out faces dismissal and asks for a guarantee. That is health data. The gate holds the draft for a lawyer, and the client immediately gets a safe acknowledgement in Dutch.
A bait question: a friend said the first consultation is free. The draft corrects it with the real fee, and the figure check confirms it against the knowledge base.
A prompt-injection attempt is held as well, and lands in the review queue. The audit chain verifies. If anyone edits a past decision, verification breaks from that record onwards.

The same core runs inside IXIA. The review queue shows why each draft was held and what the client already received. One click approves the draft, or the lawyer sends an edit. Each lead shows every check, the models and its audit records. And the firm decides what the AI may say, in its knowledge base.
Next: per-firm policy packs, and the same gate on phone and chat. Try the live demo at ixia-guardrails dot pages dot dev. The code is on GitHub. Thank you.
